about: Which coding agents exist and what repo-ai can honestly do with each. `upstream` is what the vendor documents (HEADLESS_CLI = a documented non-interactive file-editing CLI); `repo_ai` is repo-ai's state: EXECUTION (an adapter, live-verified on the development host), BLOCKED (adapter exists, an external blocker is named), PLANNED (documented headless surface, no adapter yet: nothing claims it works), UNSUPPORTED. `basis` says whether the row rests on observation on the development host or only on vendor documentation (2026-10-30 research, unverified against binaries). Generic executable names (`agent`, `q`, `cn`) are not used for detection: they collide with unrelated tools.

providers.name: Claude Code
providers.note: Isolated provider from 0.10.0 (macOS live; Linux by tests). Own login, file tools only, per-run isolation probe.
providers.account: Claude subscription or API key

providers.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
providers.note: Live-verified; its login token is readable by a model with shell access (disclosed).
providers.account: ChatGPT plan or API key

providers.name: Google Antigravity CLI
providers.note: Live-verified on macOS only (needs the read-restricted real HOME).
providers.account: Google account

providers.name: OpenCode
providers.note: Local, loopback-only model endpoints only (account-free); macOS. Cloud models through this adapter are refused.
providers.account: none (local model)

providers.name: OpenCode over ACP
providers.note: The same OpenCode driven over the Agent Client Protocol (`opencode acp`) under the `opencode` isolation: sandbox, scratch HOME, deny-by-default inline config, loopback-only model endpoint; macOS. ACP is a control channel, not a boundary: edits are checked in the workspace afterwards.
providers.account: none (local model)

providers.name: IBM Bob
providers.note: Live-verified on an earlier pre-release; not re-run for 0.10.0.
providers.account: IBM Bob entitlement

providers.name: Qwen Code
providers.note: Gemini-CLI fork with the cleanest headless contract (result event, distinct exit codes for turn/budget limits, auto-edit mode = edits without shell approval). Local: OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1, any non-empty OPENAI_API_KEY. Watch for stale exported OPENAI_BASE_URL overriding settings.
providers.account: OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_MODEL (alias QWEN_MODEL) for OpenAI-compatible; modelProviders in ~/.qwen/settings.json; /auth interactively. Qwen OAuth

providers.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
providers.note: `gh copilot` (suggest/explain extension) is NOT an editing agent; the standalone `copilot` binary is. Install page says a Copilot subscription is needed, but the auth + BYOK pages state GitHub auth is not required with BYOK; with COPILOT_OFFLINE=true + Ollama (providers.json type openai, baseUrl htt
providers.account: Env COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN > GH_TOKEN > GITHUB_TOKEN (fine-grained PAT with 'Copilot Requests' or OAuth from Copilot/gh CLI; classic ghp_ not supported); `copilot

providers.name: Goose
providers.note: Good local-model candidate (Ollama is first-class; GOOSE_INPUT_LIMIT maps to num_ctx; GOOSE_TOOLSHIM_OLLAMA_MODEL for models without native tool calling). Default GOOSE_MODE=auto means no prompts - set explicitly. No path/shell allowlist confirmed, so rely on external sandbox.
providers.account: GOOSE_PROVIDER + GOOSE_MODEL (required) and provider key env vars; keyring by default, GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING=1 for headless with env credentials. Ollama provide

providers.name: Cline CLI
providers.note: Headless auto-triggers on --json, piped stdin or redirected stdout. Auto-approve defaults TRUE (dangerous default). Has the best config/data isolation flags of the OSS set. Ollama/LM Studio provider IDs documented; account-less BYOK not explicitly stated (medium).
providers.account: `cline auth -p <provider> -k <apikey> -m <modelid> -b <baseurl>`; -k/--key per run; Cline Provider / ClinePass accounts optional; providers include ollama, lmst

providers.name: Factory Droid
providers.note: Best-designed tiered autonomy (--auto low == 'edits only, no shell side effects') and a documented terminal event. Ollama BYOK documented (http://localhost:11434/v1, any key, >=32k ctx) but docs never say a Factory login/FACTORY_API_KEY is unnecessary -> assume account required (low).
providers.account: FACTORY_API_KEY (generated in Factory settings). BYOK customModels in ~/.factory/settings.json (model, baseUrl, apiKey, provider) referenced as custom:<Name>-<i

providers.name: Kilo Code CLI
providers.note: 'The Kilo CLI is a fork of OpenCode and supports the same configuration options.' Better documented fail-closed run semantics than upstream (exit 0/1/124). Local Ollama not mentioned on Kilo page but inherited OpenCode provider config should work (medium). Redundant with OpenCode adapter.
providers.account: Kilo account (Kilo Gateway) or BYOK via /connect, `kilo auth`, provider.<id>.options.apiKey {env:..}; KILO_PROVIDER, KILO_<FIELD>.

providers.name: OpenHands CLI
providers.note: Local LLM: LiteLLM naming 'openai/<model>' with LLM_BASE_URL http://localhost:11434/v1 and placeholder key (local-LLM page is written for the Docker GUI; CLI applicability inferred). Forced always-approve in headless means zero in-agent permission control - only usable inside an external sandbox.
providers.account: LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL, LLM_BASE_URL (model/base_url only applied with --override-with-envs); `openhands login` for OpenHands Cloud (optional).

providers.name: Continue CLI
providers.note: Clean 'ask => excluded in headless' semantics (fail-closed). Ollama via config.yaml `provider: ollama` is the same format as the IDE extension (not verified on CLI docs) - treat local/account-less as medium-low until tested.
providers.account: Local config.yaml with provider keys via ${{ secrets.X }}/env; CONTINUE_API_KEY for Hub configs in CI; login gating reportedly removed (mirror commit - low).

providers.name: Aider
providers.note: Single-shot edit-format model (not an agentic tool loop); you must name files to edit (or rely on repo-map + add requests, which need confirmation -> --yes). Ollama: OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:11434, model ollama_chat/<m>; Ollama defaults to 2k ctx (aider sizes num_ctx per request). Auto-commi
providers.account: Provider env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ...), OLLAMA_API_BASE (+ optional OLLAMA_API_KEY), OpenAI-compatible via OPENAI_API_BASE; every flag also

providers.name: Cursor CLI (agent)
providers.note: Binary now documented as `agent` (cursor-agent is the legacy name). Requires Cursor account/API key; no local model support.
providers.account: CURSOR_API_KEY / --api-key; `agent login`; CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN/--auth-token (ACP page).

providers.name: Crush
providers.note: Local Ollama documented (base-url http://localhost:11434/v1/). No structured output and undocumented permission semantics in run mode make it weaker for a ledgered integration; would need empirical verification before use.
providers.account: Provider API keys via env/config; Charm 'Hyper' subscription provider optional; local providers type ollama/lmstudio/llamacpp/omlx/litellm/completions.

providers.name: Amp
providers.note: Execute mode and SDK consume PAID credits only (ad-supported Amp Free not usable non-interactively); Amp Free allowance being reduced (2026-05-23). No local/BYOK models. Requires account.
providers.account: AMP_API_KEY (sgamp_ access token from Settings); `amp login` session token rejected for scripts.

providers.name: Augment (auggie)
providers.note: Requires Augment account (session token tied to user); non-interactive may be disabled by enterprise agreement. No local models.
providers.account: `auggie auth login` then `auggie token print` -> AUGMENT_SESSION_AUTH='<json>'.

providers.name: JetBrains Junie
providers.note: EAP. Headless page shows --auth token in the canonical example; BYOK-only headless run not shown. No documented per-tool permission control in headless.
providers.account: Junie token (--auth, from junie.jetbrains.com/cli), --auth-license, JetBrains account; BYOK flags --anthropic-api-key, --openai-api-key, --google-api-key, --gro

providers.name: Kiro CLI (formerly Amazon Q Developer CLI)
providers.note: Amazon Q Developer CLI has been rebranded to Kiro CLI (Nov 2025); `q`/`q chat` remain as compatibility aliases; open-source Q CLI frozen at v1.19.7. Headless requires a paid Kiro subscription API key. No local models.
providers.account: KIRO_API_KEY (headless; only Kiro Pro/Pro+/Pro Max/Power subscribers).

providers.name: Devin CLI
providers.note: Two surfaces: (1) Devin CLI = local headless editing (EXECUTION, account required, frontier/SWE models only, no local models); (2) Devin cloud sessions API = REMOTE_SERVICE (POST /v1/sessions legacy; v3 current). accept-edits mode is a clean 'edits only' policy, but no JSON stream for -p.
providers.account: `devin auth login [--force-manual-token-flow]`; WINDSURF_API_KEY (ACP). Cloud API: bearer personal/service key against api.devin.ai.

providers.name: Roo Code
providers.note: DISCONTINUED: RooCodeInc/Roo-Code archived 2026-05-15 (read-only); extension/Cloud/Router shut down; docs.roocode.com redirects to a 404. Do not integrate. Community fork 'Zoo Code' exists (unvetted).

providers.name: Windsurf
providers.note: IDE host without a documented headless execution surface.
